pairs.subject: document-text-extraction
pairs.evidence: crates/apps/extractor/src/lib.rs:1 This context runs declarative CSS-selector rule sets over fetched or stored HTML to produce structured field records, and crawls link graphs. It never turns a foreign byte container (PDF, office file, scanned page) into human-visible text, so there are no text layers, unreadable regions, recognition paths, container expansions or emitted markup for the subject to govern; a search of crawl/ and extractor/ for pdf, docx, xlsx and text_layer found nothing (title/excerpt text comes from pumper_core::crawl, outside this context).

techniques.evidence: crates/apps/extractor/src/lib.rs:1916 The closest analogue is source mode listing missing or unreadable stored HTML bodies per key instead of writing null records. That is whole-artifact absence, not partly readable regions inside one document, so the precondition does not hold (the spirit of a list over a count is honoured anyway).

crates/apps/extractor/src/lib.rs:640 The closed status set here is selector-binding status per field (Matched/ContainerEmpty/Empty/Error), not text yield per document region. That is web-scraping selector-drift territory, not extraction-yield banding.

crates/apps/extractor/src/lib.rs:1808 The only escalation is the core fetcher's http→browser tier, which works at the fetch layer and is judged on a structured tier verdict. There is no cheap text extractor with an OCR/recognition path behind it.

crates/apps/extractor/src/lib.rs:2681 The only markdown mention is a test fixture field of the core FetchOutcome. The context emits JSON records, never Markdown or other lightweight markup built from document text.

crates/apps/extractor/src/induce.rs:21 The caps here bound run scope (pages, snapshots, records), not repeat or reference expansion inside a container reader. HTML parsing is delegated to core with no repeat-count construct to materialize.

pairs.registryProposal: The golden path's use_when could say explicitly that selector/rule-based structured extraction from HTML (web-scraping) falls outside the subject, or name the border with web-scraping in 'Where this subject stops'. Otherwise the word 'extractor' pulls scraping contexts into this subject by token match.
